reader.requirement: After a successful CLOSE without REEL/UNIT (plain, WITH LOCK, WITH NO REWIND) of a sequential file, the file is no longer in an open mode and no longer associated with its connector: every following READ/WRITE/REWRITE/CLOSE answers the not-open statuses 47/48/49/42, and a following OPEN (any mode) succeeds as on a closed file (38 only after WITH LOCK); a CLOSE REEL/UNIT on a non-reel medium leaves the file open (GR3 F).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 85 the PHYSICAL file is marked closed-with-lock, from 2002 the connector (what a later OPEN refuses with 38); the removal from open mode (FileConnector.Close) is the same code

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Dialect|CobolVersion in FileRegistry.cs (Close, CloseByFormat, CloseCell, SharedClose, CloseWithLock), FileConnector.cs (Close, Status setter), CloseTable14.cs, and FlagConformancePass.VisitCloseStatement: the plain CLOSE path consults the edition nowhere; only CloseWithLock does.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the open-mode removal and connector dissociation are one code path; only the scope of the WITH LOCK lock (physical file at 85, connector from 2002) differs, which is GR3 E's matter, not GR7's

reader.notes: FileConnector.Close clears _openMode, ModeKnown and the run-unit file lock in a finally, and SharedClose drops the connector from the physical file's open set, so every later statement sees a closed connector. The probe drove every verb after CLOSE, the WITH LOCK form, an absent optional file and reopen in all three modes; all match the 1985 statuses.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR1-GR8 and table 1 (C, E, F, H). Probes beyond the reader's (refute-1985-025/src/k7a.cob, k7ext.cob, run at --std 85): the last-READ anchor does not survive a CLOSE (OPEN I-O, READ, CLOSE, OPEN I-O, REWRITE -> 43, next READ delivers record 1); CLOSE A B with A not open -> A=42 B=00 and READ B after -> 47 (GR8 separate closes); CLOSE WITH NO REWIND on disk -> 07, then READ 47, reopen 00 at record 1 (table 1 C,H); after CLOSE B a second SELECT on the same physical file opens EXTEND 00 and its write is read back; CLOSE WITH LOCK then OPEN of the other connector -> 38; an EXTERNAL file and a GLOBAL file closed in a contained program are closed for the container (WRITE -> 48, reopen 00). cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR7 (the text is in GR7).
